bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices guide. No manufacturer manual exists for this model, so we built this from general best practices for this type of firearm. It does not represent manufacturer data. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take a firearm further apart than this guide goes unless its maker documents it.
cleanIntro:
No manual from SCT exists for this model, so this guide works from what is true of every pistol of its kind and asks you to look before it asks you to do anything. It clears the pistol, then strips it only if yours shows one of three takedown controls that come apart the same way on every pistol that has them. If yours shows none of them, the slide stays on and the pistol is cleaned locked open — that is a complete clean, not a lesser one.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 9mm. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Magazine out first, then the slide
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the grip before you touch the slide. Then pull the slide fully back and lock it open on the slide stop if your pistol has one; if it will not lock, hold it back. The order is the whole point: working the slide with a magazine still in puts a fresh round in the chamber, and that is the classic way an empty pistol stops being empty.
steps.prose: If the magazine will not come out, stop and contact SCT, with the pistol pointed somewhere safe.

steps.title: Look, then feel — and do it twice
steps.action: With the action open, look into the chamber and down into the empty magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber: a cartridge that hides in a dark chamber cannot hide from a finger. Close the action under control, open it again, and check the same way a second time.
steps.prose: ⛔ If anything will not come out, stop: never pry it out with a tool, and contact SCT with the gun pointed somewhere safe.

steps.title: Which takedown does yours have? Look before you touch
steps.action: With the pistol empty and the slide locked open, look at the frame just above the trigger. One of three things decides your next step: two small serrated tabs, one on each side of the frame just above the front of the trigger guard; a single lever on the left side of the frame, made to rotate; or a trigger guard whose front end is made to pull down away from the frame. Follow only the step written for what you see, and skip the other two.
steps.prose: ⛔ If you see none of these, more than one, or you are not sure, this is where your strip ends: leave the slide on and go straight to the cleaning steps, which work with the pistol locked open. Never press a trigger, push on a pin or press a button to find out how a pistol comes apart.

steps.title: Two tabs: release the striker, then slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Only if your pistol has the two takedown tabs. Let the slide run forward, point the muzzle at a safe backstop, and press the trigger once — on pistols built this way the striker has to be released before the slide will come off, and you will hear it click. Then grip the pistol so your fingers draw the slide back a few millimetres, pull both tabs down with your other hand and hold them there, and let the slide run forward off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: ⛔ Only after the chamber has been proven empty twice. If yours is a rimfire (.22) pistol, do not press the trigger: stop here and clean it with the slide on. If the slide will not move forward with both tabs held down, let go and stop — never force it.

steps.title: A takedown lever: turn it down, then ease the slide off
steps.action: Only if your pistol has a takedown lever. Rotate the lever down until it stops, usually about a quarter turn. Some pistols let it turn with the slide locked open and others only with the slide forward, and some also have a small button on the right side of the frame that has to be held in while the lever turns. Once it has turned, hold the slide, let it run forward under control, and ease it off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: ⛔ If the lever will not turn by hand either way, stop here and clean the pistol with the slide on. Never use a tool on the lever, and never press the trigger to make it move.

steps.title: A pull-down trigger guard: slide back, up and off
steps.action: Only if the front of your trigger guard pulls down. Pull the front of the trigger guard down; on most pistols built this way it then tips a little to one side and rests against the frame, holding itself open. Draw the slide all the way back, lift its rear end up off the frame, and ease it forward off the barrel. The barrel stays fixed to the frame and the recoil spring stays on the barrel — on this pattern neither is taken out.
steps.prose: Push the trigger guard back into place once the slide is off, so it cannot catch on anything while you clean.

steps.title: Tabs or lever: spring and barrel out of the slide
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. The recoil spring and its guide rod sit under the barrel and are still under some pressure: push the guide rod gently forward, lift its rear end clear of the barrel, and let it out slowly under your thumb. Note which way round it sat — which end faced the barrel — because it goes back the same way. Then lift the barrel out by its chamber end.
steps.prose: A pull-down trigger guard pistol skips this step: its barrel stays where it is.

steps.title: That is the whole strip
steps.action: Nothing else comes apart. The firing pin or striker, the extractor, the sights and everything inside the frame stay exactly as they are — on a pistol with no published procedure, those are work for SCT. Lay the parts out in the order they came off, on a clean cloth, away from the edge of the bench.
steps.prose: If any part came loose that this guide did not ask for, stop and contact SCT before you put the pistol back together.

steps.title: The bore, from the chamber end whenever you can
steps.action: With the barrel out, push a brush wet with bore solvent through from the chamber end, a few passes, then dry patches until they come out clean. If your barrel stayed in, lock the slide open and feed a pull-through cord in at the chamber through the ejection port, or work from the muzzle with a rod guide so the rod never rubs the crown. Finish with a lightly oiled patch for storage, and run a dry patch through before you shoot.
steps.prose: The crown — the edge of the muzzle — is what decides where the shot goes; a rod dragged across it does lasting harm.

steps.title: Breech face, rails and the feed ramp
steps.action: Wipe the breech face — the flat at the back of the slide where the cartridge sits — and the slide's rails and the frame's rails with a cloth and a little solvent, using a small nylon brush on the carbon. Wipe the feed ramp at the bottom of the chamber mouth until it is smooth and bright. Use solvent sparingly and keep it out of the frame's internals and the firing-pin hole: what runs in there cannot be wiped back out.

steps.title: Oil lightly where metal slides on metal
steps.action: A thin film of gun oil goes on the slide rails, the frame rails, the outside of the barrel where it rubs the slide, and the barrel's locking surfaces. A drop is enough on each; wipe off anything that runs. No oil goes into the firing-pin hole or into the frame from the outside.
steps.prose: Too much oil collects grit and, in the cold, slows the parts it was meant to help.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the slide, the frame and the barrel for cracks, the recoil spring for kinks or a broken coil, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for SCT.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until SCT has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the SCT 19, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from SCT exists for this model, so nothing about the inside of it can be known from a document. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to SCT, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush wet with bore solvent, from the chamber end whenever the barrel is out
Dry patches until clean, then a lightly oiled patch for storage
A dry patch through before the next shot

cleaning.name: BREECH, RAILS & FEED RAMP
tasks: Breech face wiped, carbon off with a nylon brush
Slide rails and frame rails wiped
Feed ramp wiped smooth and bright
⛔ No solvent or oil into the firing-pin hole or the frame's internals

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A thin film on the slide rails and the frame rails
A drop on the barrel where it rubs the slide, and on its locking surfaces

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly: Tabs or lever: the barrel back into the slide, then the recoil spring and guide rod back under it, the same way round as they came out.
Tabs or lever: the slide back onto the frame rails from the front and drawn fully back — it should glide without catching. On a lever pistol, turn the lever back up until it stops.

Pull-down trigger guard: trigger guard down, the slide fitted over the barrel from the front, drawn fully back, its rear lowered onto the frame and let run forward; then the trigger guard pushed back into place.
Work the slide several times by hand with an empty magazine in: it should run smoothly, and lock open on the empty magazine if your pistol has a slide stop.
Take the magazine out again before the function check.
fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber empty. Work the slide: it runs fully back and returns fully forward, and it locks open on an empty magazine if your pistol has a slide stop. Any safety or decocker you can see moves through each of its positions on the empty pistol. This check never asks you to press the trigger — whether a pistol of unknown design tolerates dry firing is a question for SCT.
